purpose: Regular update checklist and archive of source URLs used in Cyprus Labor Watch public data. When a source is used for a public record, keep the exact URL, title, publisher, date, source type, and related data file here.
archive_policy: Prefer stable article, report, official statement, or union statement URLs over category pages.
Use official/public bodies, union statements, and established news as publishable sources.
Treat social media and witness accounts as leads until corroborated by a union, official/public body, established news outlet, or report.
For island-wide or city-wide actions without exact venues, use area centroids and mark the location_basis clearly.
When possible, save external PDF/HTML snapshots outside the repo for long-term archiving; this file records live URLs and metadata.

launch_dataset.period_focus: late 2025 through May 2026 for current individual records, plus individual workplace-death backfill to 2015 and official/research fatality baselines shown as context only
coverage_notes: Whole-island coverage is represented with neutral district / area labels.
Island-wide labour actions use area-centroid placement and explicit location_basis notes.
No public current-labour-arrest record is included at launch; the Ahmet Tugcu record is marked released based on follow-up reporting.
Northern Cyprus coverage is supplemented with Turkish-language sources in data/northern-incidents.json.
data/workplace-deaths-backfill.json now contains only individual worker-death records with stable public sources and finite coordinates.
Official/research workplace-death totals are shown in the app context panel with links; no aggregate fatality markers remain in the map datasets.

work_related_deaths_source_review.focus: Purpose-specific Turkish-language resources for work-related deaths, using is cinayetleri, olumlu is kazasi, is kazasi hayatini kaybetti, isci olumu, KKTC, Kuzey Kibris, and Guney Kibris search patterns.

Latest processed bucket: 2018-07, decremented by one after adding Dimitris Zinonos's Kapsalos truck-crush death; current new July 2018 lead is complete.

coverage_notes: Turkish-language searches produced the strongest current-period leads for union arrests, police summons, and anti-union pressure.
Greek-language searches in this pass produced mostly legal and general labour-rights context, not a high-confidence recent Greek-language primary event lead.
Employer-retaliation claims should not be promoted from lead to public record until the record has either a primary union statement plus corroboration, or an official/legal/court/public-body source.
